title: The half-length uniqueness conjecture for bi-roots
source: Giuseppa Castiglione, Gabriele Fici and Antonio Restivo, “Primitive Sets of Words”, arXiv:2005.10668 (2020). https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.10668
statement:
Let $w$ be a primitive word. A **bi-root** of $w$ is a primitive pair $\{x,y\}$ whose concatenations include $w$. **The half-length uniqueness conjecture.** The word $w$ has at most one bi-root $\{x,y\}$ such that

$$
|x|+|y|<\frac{|w|}{2}.
$$

The preceding theorem proves the analogous uniqueness statement under the stronger bound $|x|+|y|<\sqrt{|w|}$. The supplied text presents the half-length bound as a problem related to the first conjecture, but gives no resolution.
summary: A primitive word w over a finite alphabet has at most one bi-root of at most half its length: if X and U are primitive pairs (two-element bases of 2-maximal submonoids) that both generate w, and twice the total length of each is below |w|, then X = U. This is the half-length uniqueness conjecture of Castiglione, Fici and Restivo, who proved uniqueness only under a square-root length bound. The proof establishes their additive conjecture in a stronger form: two distinct primitive pairs generating the same primitive word have total length at least |w| + 3. It folds the two generator graphs, glues them along the path of w into a graph of rank at most 3, shows that in rank 3 a cycle of the incidence graph would give w a period, so that the incidence graph is a forest and the bound follows by counting, and treats the remaining case by recoding w through first returns and a weighted induction on length that changes the alphabet. Lean states primitive words, generated submonoids, 2-maximality and primitive pairs literally.
paste_summary: Proved. A primitive word has at most one bi-root (primitive pair generating it) whose total length is less than half the length of the word; more strongly, two distinct bi-roots of a primitive word w have total length at least |w| + 3. This settles the half-length and additive conjectures of Castiglione, Fici and Restivo, Primitive Sets of Words (arXiv:2005.10668).
